notes:
Gaia DR3 3730485894679948928: candidates_found; one of the final 11 shortlisted HVS candidates under relaxed criteria (T:p17-b16), with only minor Nper/pmRA issues noted (T:p18-b5).
Gaia DR3 3488721051716722048: candidates_found; retained in the final 11-star shortlist (T:p17-b16; T:p18-b6).
Gaia DR3 1451652599056932480: candidates_found; retained in the final shortlist although the paper notes an unusual decrease in RPlx (T:p17-b16; T:p21-b0).
Gaia DR3 6884930019709368576: candidates_found; retained in the final shortlist, with Nper and e_pmDE issues noted (T:p17-b16; T:p21-b1).
Gaia DR3 4715594303954641920: candidates_found; retained in the final shortlist, with only a small local IPDgofha excess noted (T:p17-b16; T:p21-b2).
Gaia DR3 4294774301679435776: candidates_found; retained in the final shortlist despite local epsi/sepsi and Galactic-plane concerns (T:p17-b16; T:p21-b3).
Gaia DR3 6620452702488805504: candidates_found; retained in the final shortlist despite a global Nper deficit (T:p17-b16; T:p21-b5).
Gaia DR2 5822236741381879040: candidates_found as object B; the paper explicitly says its high RV is confirming its HVS status (T:p6-b5), although it is outside the >700 km/s shortlist.
D6-3: follow_up because it was one of the three D6 HVS candidates from Shen et al. (2018) (T:p2-b4; T:p18-b0); it is also retained in the current 11-star shortlist despite the zero RV noted (T:p17-b16).
D6-1: follow_up because it was one of the Shen et al. (2018) D6 HVS candidates (T:p2-b4; T:p18-b1); current paper retains it in the 11-star shortlist (T:p17-b16).
D6-2: follow_up because it was previously identified as a D6 HVS candidate by Shen et al. (2018) and by Scholz (2018) (T:p18-b2; T:p5-b3); it remains in the current shortlist (T:p17-b16).
Gaia DR2 3841458366321558656 / Gaia DR3 3841458366321558656: follow_up because it was previously selected as a high-priority HVS candidate and listed by Scholz (2018) (T:p18-b4); it remains in the current 11-star shortlist (T:p17-b16).
Gaia DR2 6097052289696317952 / Gaia DR3 6097052289696317952: follow_up because it belonged to the preceding Scholz (2018) DR2 HVS-candidate sample (T:p3-b7); current paper studies it in DR3 but it fails many checks and is not in the final 11, which does not affect follow_up status.
LP 40-365: follow_up because it was previously a well-measured HVS (T:p4-b3); the current paper also says the high RV confirms its HVS status (T:p6-b5).
Gaia DR3 3507697866498687232: follow_up as object D because it was included in the HVS search of El-Badry et al. (2023) (T:p6-b5); it appears among the 72 nearby extreme candidates but is not retained in the final shortlist.
Gaia DR3 5703888058542880896: follow_up as object E because Igoshev et al. (2023) listed it as an HVS WD (T:p6-b5); current boundness is not required for this category.
S5-HVS1: excluded because the paper states it is 'not included in this study' (T:p6-b0). The 72-object group is not treated as candidates_found wholesale: the final text says no convincing candidates were left (T:p15-b5), and the abstract's 'at least some' is not an explicit claim covering every member (T:p1-b6). Only the explicit 11-star shortlist and individually supported positive confirmations are counted. The paper defines an HVS as unbound to the Galaxy (T:p1-b12).

Gaia DR3 3730485894679948928: Target identified as No.62 = Gaia DR3 3730485894679948928 = LSPM J1257+0715 in Table 2 (I:p19-b0) and Sect. 3.6 (T:p18-b5). The supplied material does not report RA, Dec, distance, galactocentric radius, or a DR3 radial velocity for this object; its Table 2 RV entry is "...". The reported vtan_g ≈814 km/s (text: >800 km/s) is a Galactocentric tangential velocity, not the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed, so it was not recorded as galactic_rest_frame_velocity.

Gaia DR3 3488721051716722048: Target is No. 29 = Gaia DR3 3488721051716722048. Table 2 lists its RV as "..." (no value), and its vtan_g≈800/804 km/s is a Galactocentric tangential velocity, not a total Galactic rest-frame speed, so it was not extracted as galactic_rest_frame_velocity. No right ascension, declination, heliocentric distance, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probabilities are reported for this star.

Gaia DR3 1451652599056932480: For Gaia DR3 1451652599056932480 (No. 32 in Tables 2 and 3), the paper gives Gaia DR3 proper motions and parallax, plus a previous Gaia DR2 parallax. It does not report right ascension, declination, a parallactic distance value, or a radial velocity for this star (the RV entry in Table 2 is "..."). The tabulated vtan = 983±174 km/s and vtan_g = 741 km/s (T:p19-b0 / I:p19-b0) are tangential velocities, not the total Galactic rest-frame speed, so they are not extracted as galactic_rest_frame_velocity.

Gaia DR3 6884930019709368576: Target is No. 67 = Gaia DR3 6884930019709368576 (T:p21-b1; I:p19-b0). The paper reports a Galactocentric tangential velocity vtan_g, not the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed, and Table 2 gives no radial velocity for this object (shown as '...'), so those quantities are omitted. The distance is reported only approximately as ≈860 pc.

Gaia DR3 4715594303954641920: Target is No. 52 in the shortlist: Gaia DR3 4715594303954641920 (T:p21-b2; I:p19-b0). The paper reports its Galactocentric tangential velocity as ≈730 km/s in the text and 726 km/s in Table 2, but this is only a tangential component, not the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed, so it is not recorded as galactic_rest_frame_velocity. No right ascension, declination, distance, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this specific star; the Table 2 RV entry is "...".

Gaia DR3 4294774301679435776: Target identified as No. 10 = Gaia DR3 4294774301679435776 in Table 2 and Sect. 3.6. Table 2 lists its RV as "..." (no DR3 RV), and the paper states only three of the 72 nearest extreme candidates have DR3 RVs. No RA, Dec, distance, galactocentric radius, total Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this target. The Table 2 vtan_g = 709 km/s is a Galactocentric tangential velocity, not the total Galactic rest-frame speed, so it is not extracted under galactic_rest_frame_velocity.

Gaia DR3 6620452702488805504: Target identified as No. 42 in Tables 2 and 3 (Gaia DR3 6620452702488805504). The paper does not report RA, Dec, distance, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, total Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability for this star. Table 2 gives the Galactocentric tangential velocity vtan_g, not the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed, so it is not recorded as galactic_rest_frame_velocity. Parallax error is taken from Sect. 3.6 because Table 2 lists only the rounded parallax value.

Gaia DR2 5822236741381879040: The target is identified as object B in Sect. 2.3 and Fig. 7. The Fig. 7 insert (I:p6-b0) lists a Galactocentric tangential velocity vtan_g = 541 ± 69 km/s for object B, but this is a tangential component rather than the total three-dimensional Galactic-rest-frame speed, so it is not recorded under galactic_rest_frame_velocity. No position, parallax, distance, proper-motion components, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star. The radial velocity is only approximate, as stated in T:p6-b5.

D6-3: Target D6-3 = Gaia DR3 2156908318076164224 = LSPM J1852+6202 corresponds to No. 56 in Table 2. Table 2 lists its Gaia DR3 parallax as 0.423 mas and the text gives 0.423±0.099 mas; the DR2 comparison value is 0.427±0.126 mas (T:p18-b0). Table 2 lists the DR3 radial velocity as an ellipsis, while T:p18-b0 reports a zero RV from Shen et al. (2018). The paper gives a Galactocentric tangential velocity vtan_g ≈ >2300 km/s for this object, but not the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed, so it is not recorded as galactic_rest_frame_velocity. No right ascension, declination, distance, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star.

D6-1: For D6-1 = Gaia DR3 5805243926609660032, Table 2 (T:p19-b0) lists no DR3 radial velocity (shown as ellipsis) and gives Galactocentric tangential velocity vtan_g = 1726 km/s. This is only a tangential component, so it is not recorded as the total Galactic-rest-frame speed. No explicit right ascension, declination, or distance for D6-1 is reported in the supplied material.

D6-2: The paper reports vtan_g ≈ 1100 km/s (Table 2: 1108 km/s) and a heliocentric tangential velocity of 1031±56 km/s for D6-2, but these are tangential velocities rather than the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed, so they were not mapped to `galactic_rest_frame_velocity`. No RA, Dec, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probabilities are reported for this star. There is an internal contradiction concerning the RV: Sect. 2.5 (T:p2-b5) says D6-2 has a zero RV, whereas Sect. 1 (T:p2-b4) and Sect. 3.6 (T:p18-b1, T:p18-b2) indicate that D6-1 and D6-3 have zero RVs and D6-2 has the large RV; the Sect. 2.5 statement appears to be a printing/logical error, so the ~1200 km/s value is retained with that caveat.

Gaia DR2 3841458366321558656: The target is No. 07 = Gaia DR3 3841458366321558656 (= Gaia DR2 3841458366321558656). The paper does not report right ascension, declination, a numeric distance, Galactocentric radius, total Galactic-rest-frame three-dimensional speed, or bound/unbound probabilities for this star. The paper reports Galactocentric tangential velocities (vtan_g ≈1000 km/s) and heliocentric tangential velocity (1190±161 km/s in Table 2), but these are not the requested total three-dimensional Galactic-rest-frame speed, so they are not entered under galactic_rest_frame_velocity. Table 2 shows an ellipsis for RV, meaning no DR3 RV; the Li et al. (2018) RV is retained as an external measurement.

Gaia DR2 6097052289696317952: Target is No. 02 in Table 2 (Gaia DR3 6097052289696317952; also referred to as Gaia DR2 6097052289696317952). The paper reports a Galactocentric tangential velocity vtan_g = 729 km/s in Table 2 (T:p19-b0) and approximately 750 km/s in DR3 versus approximately 1600 km/s in DR2 (T:p5-b3), but it does not report the star's total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed; because vtan_g is only a tangential component, it is not recorded as galactic_rest_frame_velocity. No distance, equatorial coordinates, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probabilities are reported for this star. The DR3 parallax is given without an individual error in Table 2, so no parallax error is supplied.

LP 40-365: LP 40-365 is object C (T:p6-b5). The paper reports its Galactocentric tangential velocity vtan_g = 513 ± 7 km/s in the Fig. 7 insert (T:p6-b0/I:p6-b0), but this is only a tangential component, not the total Galactic-rest-frame speed, so it is not extracted as galactic_rest_frame_velocity. No exact right ascension, declination, parallax, distance, proper-motion components, galactocentric radius, total Galactic-rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this object in the supplied material. The radial velocity is only described as being of the order of 500 km/s.

Gaia DR3 3507697866498687232: Object D is Gaia DR3 3507697866498687232, corresponding to No. 72 in Table 2 (I:p19-b0) and labelled D in Fig. 7 (I:p6-b0). The paper reports a Galactocentric tangential velocity vtan_g = 865 ± 207 km/s for object D (Fig. 7 insert I:p6-b0; Table 2 I:p19-b0 gives vtan_g = 865), but because this is a tangential component rather than the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed, it is not entered under galactic_rest_frame_velocity. Table 2 shows the DR3 RV is not available (indicated by ...), so the only reported RV is the approximate external value quoted at T:p6-b5.

Gaia DR3 5703888058542880896: For the target Gaia DR3 5703888058542880896 (= object E), the paper reports only a Galactocentric tangential velocity of 620 ± 169 km/s in the insert of Fig. 7 (I:p6-b0; see also T:p6-b5). This is not the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed, and no ra, dec, distance, parallax, proper-motion components, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, total Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this object in the supplied material. No listed quantity therefore meets the scientific rules.
